s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays
salient_findings: Recurrent seizures starting at age 3 months
Upper motor neuron pattern on neurologic examination
key_facts: Age of onset of seizures: 3 months
Seizures are progressively more frequent despite antiepileptic therapy
Delayed motor and cognitive milestones
Gradual behavioral changes, including disturbed sleep and irritability
No family history of neurological disorders
No reported perinatal complications or trauma
Significant cognitive impairment on neurologic examination
Marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes
Electroencephalography showed focal abnormal brain activity
Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres
Right cerebral hemisphere atrophy and ex vacuo dilatation of the right lateral ventricle

Gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina
per_call: Congenital hemidysplasia with ichthyosiform erythroderma and limb defects syndrome
Gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina

shortlist.label: Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy, seizures, and delayed development, matching key case facts

shortlist.label: Rasmussen encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hemiparesis and seizures are key features, although the lack of inflammatory markers and specific imaging findings may lower its likelihood

shortlist.label: Hemimegalencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Involves hemispheric malformation and can present with seizures, developmental delays, and hemiparesis, consistent with some case findings

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Although typically associated with port-wine stains, it can present with seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays due to cerebral hemiatrophy

shortlist.label: Perinatal stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the cerebral hemiatrophy and subsequent developmental delays, seizures, and hemiparesis, given the early onset of symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of seizures, hemiparesis, and cognitive impairment, along with imaging findings of cerebral hemispheric atrophy and calvarial thickening, are consistent with Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome, which is characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy, often with a history of early brain injury or insult.

rejected.label: Rasmussen encephalitis
rejected.why: While Rasmussen encephalitis can cause progressive hemiparesis and seizures, it typically presents with more rapid progression and inflammatory changes on imaging, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: Hemimegalencephaly
rejected.why: Hemimegalencephaly is characterized by overgrowth of one cerebral hemisphere, which is not consistent with the atrophy seen in this patient's imaging.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Sturge-Weber syndrome typically presents with a port-wine stain, leptomeningeal angiomatosis, and calcifications on imaging, which are not mentioned in this case.

rejected.label: Perinatal stroke
rejected.why: While perinatal stroke could explain some of the patient's symptoms, the lack of reported perinatal complications or trauma and the specific imaging findings make Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome a more likely diagnosis.
